findings.observed: The RECOMMENDED menu entry (Import + History) opens CombinedImport, whose multi-sheet picker forces ONE sheet — the 'Import both — donors + their gift history' CTA exists only in DonorImport (menu: 'Import donors only'). A pilot org following the recommended path with the most common two-sheet workbook never sees the linked import.
Sarah Jones has 3 of 3 same-day $100 gifts (F-4 says all 3 insert + duplicateCandidates reports them)
"Miller" search returns 2 donors (Bob Miller / Robert Miller) — nickname/legal twins land as separate records; merge tool is the offered path
"meredith@" stored verbatim as email="meredith@" — no validation at import
formula-injection name stored verbatim: "=Sum(A1:A9)" (CSV export guard must keep escaping it)
Deceased=Y column: donor landed as a normal active donor (status=new, tags=[]) — the flag is silently discarded
Do Not Contact=TRUE column: donor landed with no suppression (status=new) — a pilot org could email a do-not-solicit donor
orphan gift's donor minted from the gift row: Sam Stranger
Margaret's refund rows (-250, "(1,000)") landed as gifts: none — negative gift handling

The gift sheet header "Donor Email" is NOT recognized by the email-column probe (isEmailHdr anchors to ^email$), so Import-both silently fell back to LINK BY DONOR NAME (screenshot 04) — whitespace/nickname/joint-name variants then mint duplicate minimal donors and split giving history. "Donor Email" is the most common real-world gift-export header.

ZERO of 2,414 imported gifts carry external_id in the DB despite a Transaction ID column on every generated row — the Import-both client payload drops it, so the F-4 external-ID cross-run idempotency contract never engages through this surface (the TXN-DUP-1 pair was deduped client-side only, and re-imports with source IDs get no DB-level protection).
